notes.text: Wikibooks library recipes can now be shown on tandra.uk's public recipe pages.
The app's font is now served by Tandra itself, so opening the app no longer contacts Google.
The app's own quality checks now catch real problems: type errors, a broken lint setup and a failing end-to-end suite are all found before a change is merged, instead of passing unnoticed.
Usage stats no longer include your list names or what you type into ingredient search.
Tandra now notes when a new account is created, so we can see how many people are joining.
Text fields no longer show a blue clear button that didn't match the app's colours.
New to-dos are private until you choose who to share them with, so friends no longer get notified about your own to-dos.
Lists you try out without an account are now a clean checklist instead of rows of missing pictures.
The app now sends standard browser security protections (content security policy, HTTPS enforcement) on every page.
Pictures for newly added items are generated again.
Todos you create with every friend switched off now stay private instead of being shared with all your friends.
Ticking off a shopping item or a todo now draws a hand-drawn green line through it, just like on the Tandra website.
Anonymous usage stats now include where people tap and how far they scroll (no page content), and no longer record usernames.
Tandra no longer asks for permission to see devices on your local network, and anonymous usage stats now work for everyone, not just on our home network.
Signing in with Google now takes you straight into the app instead of back to the login page.
Shoppingo is now Tandra. Settings saved on this device, like guest lists, start fresh.
Self-hosting Tandra no longer needs a separate auth service; MongoDB and object storage are all it needs.
You can now sign in with Google, and link Google to an existing account from Settings so you can always get back in.
Tandra now handles sign-in itself. You'll be asked to sign in once more; your username and password are unchanged.
When you choose a username, the sign-up form now tells you straight away that it can only use letters, numbers, underscores and dots.
Shoppingo is now called Tandra: the new name shows across the app, and your lists, recipes and settings are unchanged.
Kivo user import and admin password reset
Shoppingo now lives at app.tandra.uk. Sign in there and reinstall the app; your lists and recipes are all still there.
Embed Better Auth next to kivo verification
Shoppingo has moved to tandra.uk. Old links and installs send you there; reinstall the app from tandra.uk to keep getting notifications.
If you still use the old Shoppingo app icon, it now shows a banner explaining how to switch to the new one.
If you installed Shoppingo from its old address, the app now tells you to reinstall it from shoppingo-app.imapps.uk, with an install button where your browser supports one.
Tapping + or − quickly on a planned recipe's portions now counts every tap, even on a slow connection.
Trying Shoppingo without an account now looks and works exactly like the real app, opening a list no longer fails, and a clear Sign up button sits in the top bar.
Move the app host to shoppingo-app.imapps.uk
Once shoppingo.imapps.uk becomes the Shoppingo homepage, visiting it takes you straight to the app if you've signed in before.
Recipe photos load again in Firefox, and Firefox no longer keeps your sign-in token in browser storage.
Serve uploaded recipe covers with private cache control
Recipe photos you uploaded no longer go missing in the Add from recipe and Use up an ingredient lists, or after the app has been open for a while.
Lists you make before signing up no longer disappear when you refresh the page, and renaming one keeps its ticked items.
You can now try Shoppingo without an account. Your lists stay on your device, and signing up later keeps them.

Shared shoppingo links now show a preview card with the app's name and tagline, and the app itself is noindexed so the marketing site owns search.
New item pictures now sit on a clean white background, so your lists look tidier and more consistent.
Calendar todos can now be edited, are sorted by time, and show Overdue when missed; creating a list with a name that already exists now tells you.
Adding a todo with a time works again: pick the time with a proper time field.
Tags you add to a recipe are now saved instead of being silently dropped.
Voice add now shows a clear error when it can't understand you, instead of retrying endlessly in the background.
Group by aisle now actually sorts items into aisles (produce, dairy, meat and so on) instead of leaving everything under Other.
Items on your list now get sorted into their aisles automatically, including ones added earlier, so grouping by aisle no longer dumps everything under Other.
Voice input can now keep listening through pauses until you tap stop; turn it on in Settings.
Internal documentation and tooling clean-up; nothing visible in the app.
The app opens faster, and moving between pages no longer pauses for a moment.
Internal build-pipeline change; nothing visible in the app.
Internal clean-up of how lists, recipes and todos are shared; nothing should look different.
Under-the-hood upgrade of the app's data-loading library; nothing should look different.
Todos, labels, friends and push notifications respond faster as more people use the app, and the moderation report list loads in one go.
The server now checks every request more strictly and reports exactly which field is wrong, instead of failing in unexpected ways.
Lists are now tracked by an internal id rather than their name, so two people can have lists with the same name and renaming a list no longer breaks links or queued offline changes.
Browsers with Chrome's WebMCP trial, such as Gemini in Chrome, can now be asked to show your lists and add items or recipe ingredients to them.
You can now plan recipes for each day of the week from the Calendar's menu, and add everything you need for the week to a shopping list in one go.
You can now add several items to a list by speaking, for example "two loaves of bread, milk and a dozen eggs", and check them before they are added.
Shopping lists can now be grouped by supermarket aisle (produce, dairy, bakery and so on); items sort themselves and you can change any item's aisle from its edit screen.
Heavy use of the AI recipe features is now rate-limited per person with a clear "try again in a few minutes" message, and repeated ingredient-substitute lookups are instant.
Saving a new recipe is now instant; its suggested tags appear a few seconds later instead of making you wait.
Recipe photo uploads are now limited to 10 MB, converted to a lightweight format, and only visible to people who can see the recipe.
Logging out now removes your lists and any unsent changes from the device, so the next person who signs in on it can't see them.
Recipe import can no longer be pointed at internal network addresses, and oversized or slow downloads are cut off.
Creating a list with a name you already use now tells you instead of silently making a clashing list.
Item pictures can only be generated by signed-in users, with a daily limit, so a shared list can't run up image-generation costs.
Lists load faster, especially as the number of lists grows.
Two people editing the same shared list at the same moment no longer overwrite each other's changes.
Recipes from the Wikibooks Cookbook now show their photos in Discover, with the photographer credited.
You can now make your own recipes public so other people can find them on Discover, and take them down again whenever you like.
New Discover page: search thousands of recipes, narrow them by difficulty, time, tags and ingredients, preview one and add it to your own recipes in one tap.
Ingest the Wikibooks Cookbook into the discovery library
OpenSearch-backed search over a shared recipe library
Using a shared list with someone else in real time no longer causes random sign-out errors or dropped updates.
Fixed edits getting stuck as "pending" when two people edit the same list item at the same time.
Shared lists now update live: when someone else adds, ticks off or removes an item you see it straight away, and you can see who else has the list open.
Items that haven't synced yet because of a bad connection now show a small clock icon until they're saved.
The "What's new" list no longer repeats the same recipe-card line under every recent version, and each version shows what actually changed in it.
Add Recipe title, ingredient name, item name, and recipe tag fields no longer trigger Chrome Android's address or credit-card autofill pop-ups on mobile.
Ingredient substitutes pop-over now closes when you scroll the recipe page, so it stops blocking the next ingredient.

Register screen now enforces the same password rule as the server (8+ characters, letters and digits only), shows the rule under the field, and surfaces the server's specific reason when registration fails instead of a generic "Registration failed".
Notifications now appear at the top of the screen instead of covering the bottom app bar.
Toggling a share switch while the list-name or todo-title field is focused no longer closes the soft keyboard on mobile.
Recipe cards now show prep time, cook time and servings instead of the share-with-people count, so you can see how long a recipe takes at a glance.

Adding a recipe's ingredients to a shopping list now starts with a portions stepper — bump it up or down and the amounts you send scale to match, instead of always using the recipe's original quantities.

Text fields across the app now request the right mobile keyboard and autocomplete behavior for what you're typing — names, searches, links, and numbers each get sensible defaults instead of a generic keyboard.
Waste Warrior no longer pops the keyboard the moment you open it — tap the search field when you're ready to type.

Recipe Detail now has one Edit button that puts the title, link, tags, details and instructions into edit mode together, with a single Save and Cancel, instead of a separate edit toggle for each section.
The recipe-creation "Import from a link or add manually" choice now opens as a bottom sheet instead of a full page, with Cancel only at the bottom.
Recipes now offer AI-suggested substitutes for any ingredient — tap the swap icon next to an ingredient to see a few alternatives.
Recipes can now record prep time, cook time, servings and difficulty — editable when creating or editing a recipe, and prefilled automatically when importing from a link.
Scrolling through a recipe's ingredients and steps no longer randomly triggers pull-to-refresh.
Importing a recipe from a link no longer jumps the page back to the top and pops the keyboard — you can see what was imported right away.
Adding a recipe's ingredients to a shopping list now combines a near-duplicate (like "eggs" and "large eggs") into one line with the total quantity, instead of creating a second row.

Swiping to delete a shopping list item, recipe ingredient, or draft ingredient now only reveals the Delete button again — you always have to tap it to confirm, so a stray swipe can't delete something by accident.
Recipe edit and delete buttons are hidden while you pick ingredients to add to a shopping list, so you can't tap them by accident.
Swiping to delete a shopping list item now works on the first try.
Tap the version number to see what's new — every release, what changed in it, and a dot when there is something you haven't read yet.
